A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete and readable, including their appendices. Despite the new CriticalKV title and substantial reorganization, the same problem formulation, algorithms, proofs, and retained experiments can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original Needle-in-a-Haystack and LongBench experiments on Llama and Mistral, together with empirical perturbation and distance-metric analyses.

after.justification: v2 reports original Ruler, LongBench, SCBench, efficiency, sensitivity, and perturbation results in the main text and appendices.

M1.justification: The two-stage selection procedure, attention-plus-projected-value scoring, and perturbation objective remain unchanged. HeadKV supplies another integration setting; chunked prefilling supplies an additional evaluation protocol. The newly described fused Triton kernel computes the existing metric rather than introducing a different selection rule.

E1.justification: v1 evaluates two needle-retrieval tasks and 16 LongBench datasets. v2 substantially expands synthetic coverage to 13 Ruler tasks, including word extraction, variable tracking, and additional retrieval variants, and adds three SCBench multi-turn QA tasks. LongBench and both compression scenarios remain represented.

E2.justification: SnapKV and AdaKV remain, while HeadKV becomes a third extensively evaluated host and comparator. v2 adds evaluated H2O, PyramidKV, DuoAttention, and OBCache comparisons in Figure 2 and Appendices B.1 and D.2. StreamingLLM, evaluated in v1, remains discussed but disappears from the reported comparisons.

E3.justification: v2 adds Qwen2.5-32B and substantial new protocols: SCBench contexts truncated to 100K with multiple dialogue turns, latency measurements across batch sizes and context lengths, and chunked prefilling at 128K. The distance-metric comparison changes from v1's needle-retrieval setting to 4K Ruler. Existing LongBench dataset definitions and primary selection hyperparameters are retained.

E4.justification: v2 adds controlled alpha sensitivity and first-stage removal experiments at 10% and 20% budgets, plus empirical comparison of theoretical bounds with actual perturbations. It revises the L1-versus-L2 analysis. Conversely, v1's later-token perturbation diagnostics and some lowest-budget assumption-validation panels are removed rather than merely relocated.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. Additional averages and sensitivity results in v2 do not introduce uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: v2 adds extensive results for new tasks, models, comparators, efficiency measurements, and ablations. For example, its new SCBench comparison reports EN.QA scores of 15.71 for AdaKV and 22.14 with the proposed selection at 40% budget. Existing Llama LongBench scores largely persist. Some repeated results conflict: v2 Table 10 reverses the AdaKV-plus-method and HeadKV-plus-method LongBench scores relative to Table 2.

T1.justification: Definition 3.1, Assumption 3.4, and the principal theorems retain their mathematical substance. Their proofs move to Appendix A, while v1 Theorem E.1 becomes v2 Theorem C.1 with the same relaxed-bound argument. The new bound-tightness experiment adds empirical evidence, not a new derivation.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain formalizing critical-cache selection through output perturbation and improving existing eviction methods with the same algorithm. v2 refines the headline empirical claims to more than halving average compression loss and adds negligible-overhead and universal plug-and-play language.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive interpretations of alpha as a safeguard for sensitive architectures and of conservative but tighter perturbation bounds. It newly argues that code tasks are weak indicators of cache-eviction quality, explicitly excludes direct compatibility with attention-free eviction, and identifies multimodal applicability as untested. The limitations concerning fixed alpha and distance choice largely restate v1.

D1.justification: v2 newly provides a public-code access statement, FlashAttention-2 implementation information, A100 hardware details, and a fused Triton kernel description that avoids materializing projected values. It also documents the last-256-token approximation used for H2O. These are substantial additions to v1's existing pseudocode, hyperparameters, dataset specifications, and prompt templates.

R1.justification: v2 substantially expands positioning around offline budget allocation, multimodal compression, channel pruning, and inter-layer cache sharing. Appendices D.2 and D.4 explicitly distinguish the approach from OBCache and Wanda, and the introduction identifies DefensiveKV as a follow-up. These changes go beyond bibliographic updates.

P1.justification: v2 revises the title and abstract, rewrites the experimental narrative around Ruler and context-only compression, consolidates experimental settings, and moves proofs out of the main text. The appendices are extensively regrouped into proofs, extended experiments, analyses, and additional details, changing the document's organization substantially.

P2.justification: v2 adds introductory summary bars, dense Ruler task plots, efficiency charts, and numerous comparison and analysis tables. LongBench tables are expanded and consolidated, while perturbation displays are rearranged and reduced. The retained dataset and prompt-template tables are mostly relocated and renumbered rather than newly introduced.

improvement.justification: v2 addresses important gaps in v1: alpha ablations directly test the first-stage safeguard, efficiency measurements and kernel details support practical feasibility, and multi-turn QA tests the previously motivating unknown-future-question scenario. Broader comparisons strengthen the empirical case. New reporting errors, including inconsistent alpha tables, swapped scores in Table 10, and reversed timings between Appendix B.6 and Table 6, weaken numerical reliability but do not outweigh these substantial validation gains.
